text:
SuperMimic reproduction on Isaac Lab 3 (kit-less, MuJoCo-Warp)

 Unofficial reproduction of SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World
Model (arXiv 2610.28480) — no official code is released, so everything here is implemented from
the paper. Target experiment: the controlled LAFAN1 comparison (Fig. 4a): 40 G1-retargeted LAFAN1
clips (2.45 h), one GPU; the paper reaches evaluation normalized return 0.82 after 1.2 h on an H100.

Author: Chong Zhang (ETH Zurich). License: MIT.

 Disclaimer: this repository was speed-vibecoded in 1 hour with an AI coding
 assistant. It
 deliberately does not live under any lab's organization, because the code is too much "slop"
 for that: fast and unreviewed. Use it at
 your own risk.

 One G1 motion tracker for all 40 LAFAN1 clips, trained in only 1 GPU-hour 
 (0.95 h of training on a single RTX PRO 6000, 1.05 h including the checkpoint evaluations that
 shared the GPU): evaluation return 0.842 with 0/40 failed clips .
 For scale, the paper's PPO-in-simulator baseline does not reach return 0.82 within 18 h on up to
 8 GPUs.

 

 Solid robot: the trained policy simulated in Isaac Lab with MuJoCo-Warp. Blue ghost: the reference
motion. Clips: dance, jumps, fall-and-get-up, sprint. 

Progress and timestamps: MILESTONES.md.

 Layout

 Path What 
 --- --- 
 IsaacLab/ Isaac Lab main @ 46d6cc3 (VERSION 3.0.0), unmodified — cloned by tools/setup.sh , not tracked 
 docker/ Dockerfile : supermimic:latest = isaac-lab-kitless:main-46d6cc3 (built from IsaacLab/docker/Dockerfile.kitless ) + tmux, ffmpeg, gcc (for torch.compile ); run container.sh 
 data/ not tracked; tools/download data.sh fetches LAFAN1 G1 retargets (HF lvhaidong/LAFAN1 Retargeting Dataset ) and the G1 URDF/meshes, then builds g1 29dof.xml (MJCF) and the USD 
 supermimic/ implementation (see below) 
 tools/ setup, asset conversion, tests, benchmark, plotting, rendering, failure analysis 
 checkpoints/ lafan1 g1 it10000.pt : trained policy + world model (see below) 
 logs/ / not tracked: train log.csv , eval.csv , checkpoints, stdout 
 results/ success curve and highlight GIF (full videos are rendered locally with tools/render.py ) 

 Setup

Neither Isaac Lab nor any data is included in this repository; the steps below fetch them.

 Requirements: Linux, an NVIDIA GPU (tested: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, driver 580 / CUDA 13),
Docker with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit ( docker run --gpus must work), 20 GB of disk for the
images and 0.2 GB for the data.

Physics: Newton with the MuJoCo-Warp solver ( NewtonCfg(MJWarpSolverCfg(...)) ), no Kit, no PhysX;
50 Hz control, 4 substeps of 5 ms, implicitfast integrator, MuJoCo collision pipeline.

 Result (LAFAN1, 40 clips, one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell)

Evaluation return 0.842 with 0/40 failed clips at 0.95 h of training (iteration 10000; paper: 0.82

Times exclude the checkpoint evaluations, which ran on the same GPU during training (8 and 11 minutes
deducted; method in the figure footnote and tools/plot.py ). Including them: 1.05 h for v2; 1.24 h and
1.47 h for v1.

install.title: Setup
install.html:
Neither Isaac Lab nor any data is included in this repository; the steps below fetch them.

Requirements: Linux, an NVIDIA GPU (tested: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, driver 580 / CUDA 13), Docker with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit (docker run --gpus must work), ~20 GB of disk for the images and ~0.2 GB for the data.

Physics: Newton with the MuJoCo-Warp solver (NewtonCfg(MJWarpSolverCfg(...))), no Kit, no PhysX; 50 Hz control, 4 substeps of 5 ms, implicitfast integrator, MuJoCo collision pipeline.

1. Isaac Lab (kit-less Docker image)

The code runs against Isaac Lab 3 main at commit 46d6cc3 (VERSION 3.0.0), unmodified, inside Isaac Lab's kit-less image (no Isaac Sim / Kit, no PhysX). Newer main commits may work but are untested.

tools/setup.sh

which is equivalent to:

git clone https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab.git
git -C IsaacLab checkout 46d6cc3d7b115906fad12efd372fbf69f4e3d3ed
(cd IsaacLab && docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.kitless -t isaac-lab-kitless:main-46d6cc3 .)
docker build -t supermimic:latest docker/     # + tmux, ffmpeg, gcc

Then start the long-lived container (repository mounted at /workspace/supermimic):

docker/run_container.sh 0 128g     # GPU index 0, 128 GB memory cap
2. Data: LAFAN1 motions and the G1 model
What Source License Goes to
40 LAFAN1 clips retargeted to the 29-DoF G1 (30 fps CSV: root pos, root quat xyzw, 29 joint angles) HF lvhaidong/LAFAN1_Retargeting_Dataset, folder g1/ CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Ubisoft La Forge) data/lafan1_g1/*.csv
G1 description g1_29dof_rev_1_0.urdf + meshes (the model the clips were retargeted to) same dataset, folder robot_description/g1/ BSD-3-Clause (Unitree) data/g1_description/

With the container from step 1 running:

tools/download_data.sh

This also caches Isaac Lab's official ground plane and textures in data/ground/. For existing datasets, run bash tools/download_ground.sh once. This avoids a startup stall in OmniClient's S3 download. No Docker rebuild is needed.

It downloads both, then converts the robot inside the container: tools/urdf_to_mjcf.py compiles the URDF into data/g1_description/g1_29dof.xml (free-floating pelvis), and tools/mjcf_to_usd.py converts that MJCF to data/g1_usd/g1_29dof/g1_29dof.usda, which Isaac Lab spawns. The conversion is offline because the kit-less importers cannot run inside an Isaac Lab process (see Deviations). Expected result:

data/
├── lafan1_g1/                  40 CSVs (dance, fallAndGetUp, fight, jumps, run, sprint, walk)
├── g1_description/
│   ├── g1_29dof_rev_1_0.urdf
│   ├── g1_29dof.xml            generated MJCF
│   └── meshes/*.STL            38 meshes
└── g1_usd/g1_29dof/            generated USD (+ payloads/)

Check: ls data/lafan1_g1 | wc -l prints 40, and the clips total 264,705 frames at 30 fps (2.45 h). tools/test_env.py checks the converted robot against the reference motions (FK vs. simulator should agree to ~1e-6):

docker exec supermimic python tools/test_env.py

usage.title: Usage
usage.html:
CPUS=0-23 ./run_train.sh lafan1_main          # training in tmux session 'lafan1_main' (optional CPU pinning)
docker exec -it supermimic tmux attach -t lafan1_main
docker exec supermimic tmux new -d -s eval_main "cd /workspace/supermimic && python supermimic/evaluate.py --run_dir logs/lafan1_main --watch"
docker exec supermimic python tools/plot.py logs/lafan1_main --out results/success_curve.png
docker exec supermimic python supermimic/evaluate.py --run_dir logs/lafan1_main --ckpt logs/lafan1_main/ckpt_014000.pt --record traj.npz
docker exec supermimic python tools/render.py traj.npz out.mp4 --clips dance2_subject1 --seconds 10

The first iterations are slow while torch.compile builds its kernels (cached in .cache/). Checkpoints are written every 2000 iterations to logs/<run>/; the eval watcher scores each on all 40 clips and appends to logs/<run>/eval.csv.

Trained checkpoint

checkpoints/lafan1_g1_it10000.pt (71 MB) is the iteration-10000 checkpoint of the 2026-11-11 run (policy and world model): normalized return 0.842, 0/40 failed clips. Evaluate it with:

docker exec supermimic python supermimic/evaluate.py --run_dir logs --ckpt checkpoints/lafan1_g1_it10000.pt

Checkpoints trained before 2026-11-11 (including community weights for the earlier version) do not load with the current code: the observation and goal sizes changed.
